The source text explicitly describes 'discrete disagreement' where 8-connected white pixels can penetrate an 8-connected black curve without intersection in 2D. It then states that to avoid this, 'opposite' types of connectivity are used, specifying that in 3D space, 6 is opposite to 26 or 18. While the text notes 'There are no analogous results in 3D space' regarding the specific 2D separation rules (4-separating vs 8-separating), it confirms the general principle that opposite connectivity types (6 vs 26/18) are the convention used in 3D to handle separation and avoid the penetration issues inherent in discrete spaces. Thus, the evidence supports the claim that opposite connectivity types are required in 3D for these topological reasons.
